name: KEPTA 3.2.1 (desktop app)
body:
### KEPTA 3.2.1 — the free desktop app

Your memory on your own machine: encrypted at rest, no account, no KEPTA server in the middle. Works with Claude, Cursor and any MCP client.

**Why this patch exists.** `app-3.2.0` shipped a dependency that GitHub flags as critical: `proxy-addr@2.0.7`, an IP-spoofing advisory about IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses inside a trusted subnet. The desktop app carries its dependencies inside the package, so a new build is the only way to hand over the closed version. This build ships **2.0.8** — read out of the packaged file, not assumed.

**Nothing else changed.** No new surface, no behaviour, no wording in the app. And one sentence about reachability, said rather than left to inference: the app never enables `trust proxy`, so there is no forwarded-header trust decision for that advisory to poison. This update closes a flagged package; it does not open a door that was shut.

**Verified before publishing, not after.** Both architectures were launched in a throwaway home folder with a fresh 64-character key: the server answered, named `3.2.1`, and reported encryption on — `node scripts/release-beweisen.mjs 3.2.1`, exit 0. The engine repository needed no matching patch: the published npm package depends only on `better-sqlite3-multiple-ciphers`, so the flagged package was never part of what npm hands out.

**Unsigned by design.** This build is ad-hoc signed (no Apple Developer ID), so macOS will warn on first launch — right-click → Open. Same as `app-3.1.5` and `app-3.2.0`.

Checksums: `SHA256SUMS.txt` covers every asset below.

name: KEPTA 3.2.0 (desktop app)
body:
### KEPTA 3.2.0 — the free desktop app

Your memory on your own machine: encrypted at rest, no account, no KEPTA server in the middle. Works with Claude, Cursor and any MCP client.

**What changed since 3.1.5**

- **The graph now keeps what it promises.** The collision pass ran four times a frame; on a dense base that was not enough. It is **eight** now, and a brute-force count over every pair — no padding, no browser — reports **0 intersecting discs at rest at 400, at 1 500 and at 3 000 notes** (`tests/lib/graphLayout.test.ts:2285`). While a 3 000-note field cools, the funnel closes from ≤ 40 pairs to 0.
- **Two sentences are gone from the README, because measurement killed them:** „3 000 nodes … at 60 fps" was never reproducible from this repository, and „1 500 notes inside the 16.67 ms budget" stopped being true after the fix — 1 500 notes need 17.5 ms while cooling. The honest ceiling for 60 fps is about **400 notes**, and the page says so.
- **The surface got its space back:** the header bar took 548 px away from the canvas at 1 440 px; it now takes none, and the density ladder runs 19 steps instead of one.
- **The design system moved to the measured ladder**, and a new guard checks the drawing scenes against the app's own stylesheet — that guard caught a film painting nodes in a colour no customer sees any more.
- **The AI key now lives in an AES envelope**, not in plain view, and the server behind the app was hardened along with the engine's.
- **A disk guard that refuses to start** (`--leicht` 2 Gi, `--schwer` 8 Gi, exit 75) and a CPU quietness probe, byte-identical with the engine repository.

**Verified before publishing, not after:** the packaged binary was run — encryption on, full-text search working, `/api/health` answering `3.2.0` on a real library of 14 701 notes. `node scripts/pruefe-native.mjs release` green for both architectures.

**Unsigned by design:** this build is ad-hoc signed (no Apple Developer ID), so macOS will warn on first launch — right-click → Open. Same as `app-3.1.5`.

Checksums: `SHA256SUMS.txt` covers every asset below.

name: KEPTA 3.1.5 (desktop app)
body:
### KEPTA 3.1.5 — the free desktop app, now without any meter

Your memory on your own machine: encrypted at rest, no account, no KEPTA server in the middle. Works with Claude, Cursor and any MCP client through the same engine that is published here as `kepta-mcp`.

**macOS · Apple silicon and Intel · free**

**Check it yourself:** `SHA256SUMS.txt` is attached, one line per installer. After downloading all four, `shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS.txt` must read `OK` on every line — the builder ran that same check against these exact files before uploading, and GitHub's own server-side digests for the four assets match them.

This release is the desktop application, built from the private `kepta-app` source repository; the memory engine underneath is published here as `kepta-mcp`.

#### What changed: there is nothing to activate and nothing to run out of

The app no longer counts. Until 3.1.4 it measured some tools per day (thirteen rules: 10 chats, 5 clips, 2 computer scans, 20 profile saves, 10 dossiers and so on), gave a sealed first 24 hours, and answered a reached limit with 429 plus a link to buy a key. All of that is deleted — the counters, the trial day, the key field, the panel, the sidebar line „A key removes the limits", the toast that announced the day was over. Every tool runs for everyone, without bound, at every moment.

This was not a lock being picked; the app never locked anyone. But counting needed places to hide the tally — an authenticated state in the database, an anchor in the keychain, a hidden file outside the data folder — and a memory that is yours without supervision should not be keeping those. So the mechanism is gone rather than tuned, and a test now fails if any of it returns: twelve chat messages and twenty-one profile saves in a row all answer 200, no `X-KEPTA-Plan` header, no `/api/license` route, and nothing written to the settings any more (`tests/keine-grenzen.test.ts`).

Verified inside the shipped binaries, both architectures: the strings `Unlimited day`, `A key removes the limits`, `Daily free limit` and `kepta.pro/upgrade` appear nowhere in the packaged server or interface, and the packaged window — read over the debug port from the built `KEPTA.app` — renders the sidebar footer as **KEPTA / local · private · encrypted** and nothing else about plans or keys.

#### What stayed, because it was protection rather than payment

Loopback-only binding and the "only this computer" check, the security headers, the 1 MB body cap, the write throttle of 60 per minute and the chat throttle of 20 per minute, the 5 000-node ceiling, the privacy shield, and the recovery key with its three doorkeepers (own host, own origin, a header a foreign page cannot send). Team scopes and their roles are now switched on by an organisation's own managed file (`managed-settings.json`) instead of by a paid edition — a feature that worked before keeps working, it is no longer waiting on a key. Keys themselves belong to KEPTA Enterprise, which is a separate server under agreement; the signing module and the studio remain in the source as that tooling, and no code path in the app reaches them.

Existing installs lose nothing: old counter fields stay in the database unread and unwritten, and no data is deleted by this change.

#### Note for macOS

This build is ad-hoc signed, not notarised: on first launch macOS says the developer cannot be verified. Apple removed right-click *Open* in macOS 15, so use one of the two routes that still work — **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway**, or `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/KEPTA.app`. Once, then never again.

Nothing leaves your machine on its own: no account, no telemetry, no phone-home, no key check of any kind, and no auto-updater that would call a server. Chat only talks to a model provider you configure yourself, and the default is `localhost:11434` (Ollama).

name: KEPTA 3.1.4 (desktop app)
body:
### KEPTA 3.1.4 — the free desktop app

Your memory on your own machine: encrypted at rest, no account, no KEPTA server in the middle. Works with Claude, Cursor and any MCP client through the same engine that is published here as `kepta-mcp`.

**macOS · Apple silicon and Intel · free**

**Check it yourself:** `SHA256SUMS.txt` is attached to this release, with one line per installer. After downloading all four, `shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS.txt` must read `OK` on every line — the builder ran that same check against these exact files before uploading them.

This release is the desktop application, built from the private `kepta-app` source repository; the memory engine underneath is published here as `kepta-mcp`.

#### Security — a door the app never used is closed

The window's content policy still allowed `fonts.googleapis.com` and `fonts.gstatic.com`, although the app ships no webfont at all: every face comes from the system, through CSS variables. On an app whose whole promise is that nothing leaves the machine, an unused permission is still an open door — one added `<link>` and a first launch would fetch type from Google. The policy now reads `font-src 'self' data:`, and a test fails if a font host reappears in it.

This was checked inside the shipped binaries, not only in the source: the `KEPTA.app` in both architectures carries the tightened policy. Measured on the build machine against this exact package: every socket the running app held sat on `127.0.0.1` — fourteen of them, counting the listeners and the renderer’s keep-alive connections — and none reached any other address. The only peer it contacted was a model server on `127.0.0.1:11434` (the configured local Ollama); on a machine without one, the attempt simply fails locally. The default chat provider stays `localhost:11434` (Ollama); nothing is contacted until you point it somewhere yourself.

#### Fixed

- **The MCP install instruction pointed at an npm version that does not exist.** The registry descriptor (`server.json`) is what an MCP client reads to install the engine, and it named `kepta-mcp@3.1.3`. What npm has published under that name is **3.1.2**, so the command the registry would hand every client — `npx kepta-mcp@3.1.3` — failed with `not found`. The descriptor now names the published version, and a test pins it to the registry rather than to the app's own number. The desktop app is 3.1.4; the engine on npm stays 3.1.2 until the next engine release, and the release text says which is which.
- **A clean `npm ci` could die with `notarget`.** A version bump had replaced the string `3.1.2` wherever it stood, including inside two dependency entries, so the lockfile asked the registry for versions it has never published. Both entries name real published versions again, and `npm test` now compares every lockfile entry against the installed tree before the suite is allowed to start.
- **A packaging run no longer fakes a broken test suite.** Building the installer rebuilds the native SQLite module for Electron; the next `npm test` then failed hundreds of tests whose visible message was a trailing cleanup line rather than the cause. The test command loads the module under the running Node first and, when it cannot, names the one command that fixes it.

#### Under the hood — why the numbers here are worth reading

- **One listener per app under test, not one per request.** Supertest bound a fresh ephemeral port for every single call and released it right after the answer; with 118 parallel workers the suite began answering with statuses this app cannot produce (401 where 403 belongs, `ETIMEDOUT`, a 200 without the counter header its middleware always sets). Each app now keeps exactly one listener for the length of its file, and a test measures that. Result: 118 files / 1989 tests, green in repeated full runs and on the CI runner.
- **The documentation stopped describing an app that is not this one.** The README offered a “KEPTA Pro” tier that does not exist (what exists is KEPTA Core, free, and KEPTA Enterprise, by agreement), and it listed Windows and Linux installers as downloads while every published release carries macOS only. Both are now stated honestly, and a docs test fails if either claim comes back.
- **A speed promise that survives a busy machine.** One interaction check demanded sub-4 ms for a pointer move over 12 000 links from a single 20-move average; it fell at 5.85 ms on a loaded machine while nothing about the search had changed. It takes the median of three 60-move series now, and prints all three.

#### Note for macOS

This build is ad-hoc signed, not notarised: on first launch macOS says the developer cannot be verified. Apple removed right-click *Open* in macOS 15, so use one of the two routes that still work — **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway**, or `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/KEPTA.app`. Once, then never again.

Nothing leaves your machine on its own: no account, no telemetry, no phone-home, and no auto-updater that would call a server. Chat only talks to a model provider you configure yourself.

name: KEPTA 3.1.3 (desktop app)
body:
### KEPTA 3.1.3 — the free desktop app

Your memory on your own machine: encrypted at rest, no account, no KEPTA server in the middle. Works with Claude, Cursor and any MCP client through the same engine that is published here as `kepta-mcp`.

**macOS · Apple silicon and Intel · free**

**Check it yourself:** `SHA256SUMS.txt` is attached to this release. After downloading the four installers, `shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS.txt` must read `OK` on every line — that is the same check the builder ran against the published files.

This release is the desktop application, built from the private `kepta-app` source repository; the memory engine underneath is published here as `kepta-mcp`.

#### What is new since 3.1.2

The knowledge graph was finished.

- **A third view: Semantic.** Notes placed by what their texts mean, from a deterministic projection of your own vectors, computed on your machine. It states how much of the difference its two axes carry and what it left out.
- **Forces you can set.** Center force, repel strength, link distance, node size — four sliders that retune the running field without rebuilding it or moving your camera.
- **The graph reads as structure, not as a hairball.** Repulsion is weighted against the link springs again, so unrelated topics stand apart as islands with white space between them.
- **Links say what they claim.** Direction (who over whom), the relation as text, thickness from how many claims sit on a pair, and expired claims drawn dashed.
- **Nothing is dropped quietly.** Badges count hidden neighbours, a balance line names every gap, and a schema panel shows what the store actually holds.
- **Concepts are nodes**, with a number inside showing what they carry; groups fold with a persistent count, in both views; a term that only repeats the title of its own note is no longer treated as a concept.
- **The tree folds itself to fit its canvas** instead of cutting rows off the screen, and says so — one click opens everything again.
- **Fit-to-view really frames the whole graph**, including the strip the legend takes at the bottom.
- **Search counts its hits** and pages between them.
- **Provenance colour**: written in KEPTA, from a file, or from this computer.

#### Fixed

- A base of ~400 notes opened as a black canvas: the spring net diverged and the world grew without bound. There is a per-frame speed limit now.
- A filter left the camera zoomed out on an empty field.
- Two partial responses from the file-import preview crashed the dialog.
- At phone width the graph was given an 80-pixel strip.

#### Security

- Memories marked private are no longer readable or deletable through the agent paths.

#### Note for macOS

This build is ad-hoc signed, not notarised: on first launch macOS says the developer cannot be verified. Apple removed right-click *Open* in macOS 15, so use one of the two routes that still work — **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway**, or `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/KEPTA.app`. Once, then never again.

Nothing leaves your machine on its own: no account, no telemetry, no phone-home. Chat only talks to a model provider you configure yourself.

name: v3.1.2 — die Desktop-App ist wieder da
body:
## v3.1.2 — die Desktop-App ist wieder da. Für alle.

**Download:** `KEPTA-3.1.2-mac-arm64.dmg` (Apple Silicon) · `KEPTA-3.1.2-mac-x64.dmg` (Intel) — herunterladen, öffnen, in den Programme-Ordner ziehen. Beim ersten Start: **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway**, oder `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/KEPTA.app` (ad-hoc-signiert, nicht notarialisiert; einmal, dann nie wieder). Rechtsklick → „Öffnen" entfernt Apple in macOS 15 aus dem Menü.

**Eine verschlüsselte Erinnerung auf deinem Rechner, geteilt von jeder KI, die du nutzt.** Kein Cloud, kein Konto, keine Abo. Der Kern ist source-available (BUSL-1.1) und misst sich öffentlich: **61.5 % on LongMemEval-S** — jeder Frage-Record jedes Laufs liegt in diesem Repository (id, Typ, Fähigkeit, Urteil, Trefferzahl, Verbatim-Flag) — Frage- und Antworttexte kommen aus dem SHA-pinnten Upstream-Datensatz.

**`npx kepta-mcp ui` startet keine Browser-Oberfläche mehr** — KEPTA ist im Kern headless by design und lebt im KI-Klienten via MCP. Die App hier ist die echte Oberfläche; der Befehl zeigt jetzt den richtigen Weg (`npx kepta-mcp setup`).

**KEPTA Enterprise** (Mandanten-Gehirne, fälschungssichere Audit-Kette, Menschenschleuse, PITR) bleibt auf Anfrage.

→ Engine ohne App: `npx -y kepta-mcp setup` · Python client (MIT): pypi.org/project/kepta

name: v3.1.1 — the engine you can embed
body:
## v3.1.1 — the engine you can embed

**The whole memory engine is now an embeddable library.** `require("kepta-mcp/engine")` exports `KeptaStore`, the hybrid search engine, consolidation and indexing — build your own memory products on the exact engine KEPTA runs.

**New public record: 61.5 % on LongMemEval-S** — 500 questions, graded by a local 14B judge, one consumer GPU, zero cloud. That is 96 % of the cloud-judged number the best-funded competitor reports. Every question record of every run is committed in `tools/longmemeval/ergebnisse/` — id, type, skill, verdict, hit count and the verbatim flag; the question and answer texts come from the SHA-pinned upstream dataset — reproducible by anyone.

**Speed, measured and public:** search p95 under 100 ms at 100k memories, warm start in under a second — the search cache keys on trigger-fed generations, AND-first full-text intersect, and a delta cache that stays warm after every write.

**Unchanged:** 8 MCP tools, protocol 2026-07-28, stdio + Streamable HTTP, one encrypted SQLite file on your own machine, BUSL-1.1 (converts to AGPL-4-years-after-release). Free forever.

→ Full series and harness: tools/longmemeval/README.md
→ Python client (MIT): pypi.org/project/kepta

name: v3.0.0 — the tiers are gone
body:
Pro is gone. Everything memory-related is free and open. Enterprise by request.

## What changed
- **No tiers inside the memory** — €0, forever, unlimited: no account, no daily limits, no key. The proprietary desktop app and the Pro tier are discontinued.
- **MCP tool parity over HTTP** — `consolidate` + `forget` now work over HTTP and Python too (31 routes); the Python client reaches full 8-tool parity.
- **Search cache on a trigger-fed data generation** — 100k memories: search median **7.16 s → 46.6 ms**; the cache grows with the data (post-ingest build at 1 M: **359 s → 0.74 s**).
- **AND-first FTS + precomputed vector norms** — 1 M memories: search median **276.5 ms** on a worst-case synthetic corpus.
- **HyDE-lite** in the benchmark harness (additive declarative extensions).
- **Public benchmark records** — every question record with its verdict: LongMemEval-S **39.0 %** (3B-judge series 29.2 → 39.0) and **54.6 %** with the stronger local 14B judge, zero cloud.

Install: `npx -y kepta-mcp@3.0.0 setup` · Python: `pip install kepta==0.2.0`

name: v2.13.22 — License: BUSL-1.1
body:
## License change

**The license is now [Business Source License 1.1](blob/main/LICENSE) — replacing AGPL-3.0-or-later.**

- Every line stays public.
- Production use inside your own organization, on your own hardware, is always allowed.
- Offering the engine (or a modified version) to third parties as a hosted or managed service is reserved for a commercial license.
- Each version converts to **AGPL-3.0-or-later four years after its release**.
- The Python client under `python/` stays MIT.

## Also in this release
- Discussions opened: security feedback, benchmark methodology, ideas (https://github.com/DamianTodorovic/kepta/discussions)
- Benchmark record public: LongMemEval-S, every run committed (`tools/longmemeval/ergebnisse/`)
- Publishing workflow: robust propagation check

npm: `npm i -g kepta-mcp@2.13.22` — Metadata on npm already carries BUSL-1.1.
